niche: a state educator licensing board's 2027 formal reviews of its educator preparation programs, decided on their 2025-26 completers' first-attempt pass rates on the state's elementary literacy licensure test, whose 2026 form the board's assessment office equates itself for the first time, to the 2025 form through an anchor of twenty multiple-choice items and one rater-scored written assignment
stakeholder_role: the licensing board's director of assessment research

spine.file: the scoring contractor's 2026 written-assignment read file
spine.entity: one read of one written-assignment response: operational first and second reads, resolution reads, scoring-leader back-reads and seeded validity papers
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a constructed-response scoring system's read export)

world.geography: United States, an unnamed state (the board, its preparation programs, both testing contractors and the people are fictional)
world.org_type: state educator licensing board with its own assessment research office
invented_names: Board of Educator Standards and Licensure

driver: The decisive quantity is the second administration's score at the first administration's standard, estimated through a shared subset of which one part is judged by people, and the second administration's judges applied a harsher standard than the first, measured only on a random set of the first administration's responses with settled scores that the second judges re-judged unknowingly; the judged part has to be put back on the first standard before it carries the link, because used as judged it makes the second group look weaker and the cut too high, and dropped from the subset it leaves a link blind to the second group's real decline on what only the judged part measures, which sets the cut too low.
driver_concrete: The 2026 raw passing score is the 2026 raw score whose equated 2025 raw score rounds to the 2025 passing score, equated through the 21-item anchor with the carried-over written assignment's 2026 reads moved by the mean amount the 2026 raters scored the 2025 validity papers below their consensus scores (twice that per response, two reads), not the anchor as the 2026 raters scored it, nor the twenty multiple-choice items alone.
stump: The default path equates the 2026 form to the 2025 form through the 21-item anchor as the 2026 raters scored it and sets the 2026 raw passing score two to three points too high, sending more programs to formal review than the golden; the 2026 raters scored the carried-over written assignment's 2025 validity papers about a quarter point per read below their consensus scores, so the anchor reads the 2026 cohort as weaker than it is, and screening that item out of the anchor instead overshoots, because the cohort really did write worse; with the written assignment put back on the 2025 rating standard the anchor sets the cut the golden takes.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms both contractors' score files, keys every attempt to the candidate, builds the first-attempt equating samples the technical report names and equates the 2026 form to the 2025 form through the anchor by Tucker, Levine, chained linear or chained equipercentile with the written assignment as the 2026 raters scored it sets the 2026 raw passing score two or three points too high and sends more programs to review than the golden; screening the anchor for the item whose mean moved and linking through the twenty multiple-choice items sets it two points too low and sends fewer; only the anchor with its written assignment put back on the 2025 rating standard, measured by the 2025 validity papers the 2026 raters scored, files the golden set.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the new form's raw score at the old form's passing standard, estimated by common-item nonequivalent-groups equating through a mixed-format anchor, and test equating requires the anchor to be scored on the same standard in both administrations, which for a rater-scored item means measuring the raters' drift on responses with settled scores and taking it out (the field's trend-scoring problem for constructed-response anchors); swapped for a hospital's readmission rate or a utility's load with another field's nouns, there is no anchor, no rating standard and no equating, and the call has nothing to decide on.
layer1: a scoring contract changed contractors between the 2025 and 2026 administrations, each with its own score-file layout and identifiers
candidate keys across contractors through the board's educator identifier, captured at registration with gaps and typing errors
first attempt read from attempt history across both contractors and earlier years
score verification requests whose rescored releases supersede the preliminary scores
written-assignment scores built from two reads with resolution reads for non-adjacent pairs
program completer lists submitted in each program's own layout, some by academic year and some by term
candidates on two programs' lists and completers who have not yet tested

differentiation.task450: task450 v2 screens a shared subset for keyed items whose difficulty moved for the new cohort and links through those that held; here no item moved: the people scoring the one judged item applied a harsher standard, measured on settled responses they re-judged, and screening that item out is a wrong rung because the cohort really did decline on what it measures.
differentiation.task464: task464 v2 links two different instruments through a sample measured on both, by matching distributions rather than regressing; here one instrument's forms are linked through shared items across two cohorts, and the decisive move is putting the judged item back on one rating standard.
differentiation.task246: task246 takes each measurer's own fixed offset and random error out of single readings to read a prevalence below a cut-off within one survey round; here no prevalence is read off ratings: one judged item carries a link between two administrations, the judges' shared shift against the earlier standard is taken out of that item alone so the shared subset measures both groups alike, and the item is kept because the second group really differs on it.
differentiation.task266: task266 builds a completion share from competing hazards among spells still open; here nothing is censored: a test form's passing score is placed on an earlier form's standard through a shared subset whose judged part drifted.
differentiation.task202: task202 recovers the within-unit spread a record of unit averages hides, from the minority of units reporting item by item; here no spread is recovered: the judged part of a shared subset is put back on the earlier rating standard before it links two test forms.
differentiation.task449: task449 inverts the dilution a link to the wrong record puts on a share; here no records are linked: one judged item's rating standard shifted between administrations and is measured on settled responses the new judges re-judged.
differentiation.task466: task466 fits a low extreme quantile to a recent record and an older record censored at one level; here the quantity is a test score at an earlier passing standard and the correction is a rating-standard shift on one anchor item.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a per-category total of trips taken from replies to a sample handed out on each day of a fixed window, where a reply comes back only when its trip ends and collection stopped soon after the window closed, so a long trip is among the replies only if it began early enough to end before collection stopped; the categories made of long trips are restored by weighting each reply by the inverse of the share of handout days from which a trip of its length could have come back, not by the return rate of its own handout day nor by the inverse of its length.
lineage.niche: a state aviation bureau's 2027 route pitch for its regional airport, ranked on the 2026 trips from the regional service area that drove to the state's hub airport and parked there, estimated from the hub's parking entry register and a card survey whose cards come back only when the car leaves
lineage.stump: The default path expands each wave's returned cards to its quarter's entries and pitches Washington, New York and Dallas (6,513, 5,121 and 4,829 trips), because a card comes back only when its car leaves and each wave's drop boxes were taken in two days after its last handout, so the cards handed in a wave's later days came back only from short stays, and the two- to four-week winter stays that make up much of Phoenix and Tampa are thinned out of the replies; weighted for when each stay could have come back, Phoenix, Tampa and Washington lead.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-19: three isolated readers landed the call by weighting each returned card for when its stay could come back (Gate F), and the ask device was a mirror device (pair ceiling 55.5); a clustered-design hold measured on the v1 pack was dropped (73,909 returned cards put every lead over the fourth market at z 2.3 to 3.5); re-rooted fresh by the author's rule (no retirement)

notes: v2 drawn 2026-10-20 in the least-drawn ETL task type (two cards); the anchor's written assignment is the decisive organ and its drift is visible only in validity reads the contractor reports as agreement rates
